archetypes.name: trap-sequencing
archetypes.rationale: The plan's trap-chain insertion points are stated as specific line numbers per script, but a misplaced call captures the wrong prior-trap body into LARCH_QUIET_PREV_EXIT_TRAP — a silent failure mode the plan itself flags as highest-risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each of the nine denylisted scripts, locate the actual final `trap ... EXIT` registration in the file and compare it to the line number the plan cites as the insertion point for `larch_quiet_append_done_trap`. If any intermediate `trap ... EXIT` call exists after the plan's stated insertion line, the done-trap would snapshot an incomplete prior chain, producing a missing `.done` sidecar with no error signal. Pay special attention to `scripts/ci-wait.sh` (plan cites line 170), `scripts/collect-agent-results.sh` (plan cites line 307), and `skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh` (plan cites line 402) — all three have existing cleanup traps whose chain order is load-bearing. Also verify the plan's claim that `scripts/run-step5-review.sh` and `skills/implement/scripts/run-step2-dispatch.sh` have no prior EXIT trap at all, since sourcing `lib-quiet.sh` last would be wrong if a trap was registered before the source line. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: api-line-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan references lib-quiet.sh at four specific line ranges (159-178, 160, 186-199, 222-225); if any shifted in the codebase the implementation instructions produce incorrect placement, wrong argv form, or category drops with no compile-time signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `scripts/lib-quiet.sh` and verify each of the plan's line-number citations: `larch_quiet_append_done_trap` body at lines 159–178, the early-return guard at line 160, `emit_breadcrumb` argv parsing (specifically `--category=NAME` single-token vs `--category NAME` two-token acceptance) at lines 186–199, and the fixed category vocabulary enforcement at lines 222–225. Cross-check the vocabulary set the plan treats as canonical — `{progress, warn, stall, retry, escalate, wait-ci, network-flake}` — against what the file actually enforces, since a vocabulary mismatch means the plan's category assignments will silently produce `unknown-category` drops in the stream for real callers. Also verify that `larch_quiet_init` is idempotent when called in scripts that do not set `LARCH_DONE_SENTINEL` or `LARCH_STATUS_FILE`, since the plan relies on this to justify unconditional adoption in `run-step5-review.sh` and `run-step2-dispatch.sh` without byte-identical stdout/stderr regression tests. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: batch-schema-extension
archetypes.rationale: The plan invents a directory-style batch entry with a new sanitizer name and a new --input-dir flag for larch-log.sh, but does not verify these against the existing TSV format or the dispatcher's current switch cases — a schema mismatch would silently skip the breadcrumbs batch at publish time.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `scripts/larch-log-batches.sh` and extract the exact heredoc or TSV format for existing batch rows to determine whether the plan's proposed new row `breadcrumbs / replace breadcrumb-streaming` matches the column schema and whether the `extension /` notation for directory-style batches is an existing convention or a newly invented one with no parser support. Then read `scripts/larch-log.sh` and locate the dispatch logic that branches on `BATCH` and `SANITIZER` values, checking whether introducing `--input-dir` as an alternative to `--input-file` requires changes to argument-parsing sections the plan does not list as modified. Verify that the plan's partial-publish contract (skip-per-file + `Warnings` entry + caller returns 0 when at least one file succeeded) is consistent with how existing batch failures are surfaced upstream — specifically whether `PUBLISH_OK=true` is a variable the caller already checks or one the plan must introduce. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: deferred-ci-gap
archetypes.rationale: Items 4 and 7 are deferred but the acceptance criteria list make targets and agent-lint entries that depend on them; a new script file landed by PR #2786 without its allow-list entry would cause agent-lint to fail on the very CI run that merges this PR.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `agent-lint.toml` and check whether `scripts/breadcrumb-monitor.sh`, `scripts/lib-redact-streaming.sh`, and any other files already landed by PR #2786 but not yet covered by allow-list entries would cause `agent-lint` to fail on CI before item 7 is addressed. Read the Makefile and `scripts/test-implement-anti-polling-rule.sh` to verify that the acceptance criteria's `make test-breadcrumb-monitor` and `make test-breadcrumb-monitor-bash32` targets the plan defers to item 7 are not already referenced by an existing phony target or CI workflow step that would fail immediately. Also check `scripts/lint-foreground-markers.sh` to see whether the new sibling `.md` files (`scripts/breadcrumb-monitor.md`, `scripts/lib-redact-streaming.md`) that this PR creates are expected to contain any foreground-marker patterns that the linter would scan and potentially flag, since the plan does not address their markdown content relative to the linter's pattern matching. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
